user_need_match.evidence: All 3 tokio::spawn forwarding sites in main.rs (ForwardCharToSession:1033/1040, ForwardKeyToSession:1048, SendTextRawToSession:1057) replaced with fwd_tx.send() calls. spawn_forwarder (forwarder.rs:50-97) creates ONE consumer task backed by an unbounded FIFO mpsc channel. Because exactly one task reaches the SDK transport, delivery order is guaranteed. Coalescing of adjacent Text messages for the same session (lines 78-83) and flush-before-Key (line 88) preserve exact interleave order. Build: 0 errors. Tests: 195 passed (improved from 191/1). hinge_findings.concern: The entire ordering guarantee rests on this function: one consumer drains one FIFO channel. If the consumer exited prematurely (panic, recv error), subsequent fwd_tx.send() calls would silently return Err(SendError) (ignored by let _ =) and keystrokes would disappear.
hinge_findings.verified_safe_by: Consumer exits only via Disconnected/None (sender dropped). No panic paths: send_text_raw errors go to set_err (caught), sink.lock() only fails on poisoned mutex (no other holders). Popper test 4 (one tokio::spawn) and test 6 (195 tests pass) confirm the consumer does not crash under normal usage.

hinge_findings.concern: forwarder receives connect_cached() singleton — same socket as refresh_preview. Both paths serialize through rmux SDK's single actor mpsc. Risk: forwarder and refresh_preview contend on the same transport under high typing + preview refresh.
hinge_findings.verified_safe_by: rmux SDK transport is a single-actor mpsc queue (obs:45162). All requests are serialized there regardless of how many concurrent callers exist. Contention = queueing, not corruption. Acceptable latency tradeoff.

hinge_findings.concern: If two sessions interleave in the channel (session A text, session B key, session A text), flush fires correctly between them. But the check is `*s == session` — if session names differ by only one character due to a rename/typo, a stale pend could be flushed to the wrong target.
hinge_findings.verified_safe_by: Session names come from app.selected_session().session.name — a stable string derived from rmux. They do not change mid-drain cycle. Popper test: session names in the TUI are set at session creation and never mutated.

`let _ = fwd_tx.send(...)` silently discards SendError if forwarder consumer drops prematurely. Keystrokes would disappear with no user feedback.

edge_cases.scenario: rmux daemon OOM-killed and auto-restarted. CACHED_MANAGER holds old Arc. ForwardMsg consumer calls mgr.send_text_raw() → io::Error (connection refused). set_err writes the error. async_status drain surfaces 'Forward failed: connection refused' in status bar. User's keystrokes are lost silently until omega restart.
edge_cases.evidence_gathered: is_pane_stale() matches only PaneNotFound | OwnedSessionLeaseLost (not io::Error). OnceCell never re-initializes once set.

edge_cases.scenario: forwarder consumer panics (e.g., future panic from tokio runtime). Channel becomes disconnected. fwd_tx.send() returns Err(SendError) silently (let _ = ). User continues typing, keystrokes all disappear. No recovery, no user feedback.
edge_cases.evidence_gathered: Consumer has no panic paths in current code — but future additions to forwarder.rs could introduce one.
